news.title: Mumbai: BMC issues stop-work notice to Andheri demolition site over dust-control violations
news.para: In response to dust pollution violations, BMC’s K/West ward office has issued a stop-work notice to a developer. Following complaints from the Lokhandwala Oshiwara Citizens Association, a penalty of Rs 35,000 was also enforced. The civic authority identified several infractions of air pollution control guidelines during demolition operations, raising concerns among residents about potential health impacts. The police have been directed to oversee the site to ensure BMC compliance.

news.title: FSI doubled, Belagavi Cantonment set for vertical growth
news.para: Defence ministry notifies revised building by-laws, paving way for redevelopment. Revised rules allow buildings up to 16m; public to get 30 days to file objections, suggestions

news.title: Delhi government to take action against buildings violating pollution control norms: Minister
news.para: Delhi's Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa conducted a thorough inspection of pollution control measures in high-rise buildings to ensure they meet necessary standards. Highlighting the government's dedication to air quality, he warned establishments failing to comply could face significant penalties. As part of the Winter Action Plan, Sirsa urged vehicle owners to follow new emission regulations, supported by extensive monitoring teams and air quality stations throughout the city.

news.title: Over 2,500 flats booked under Delhi development body's Awas Nivesh housing scheme
news.para: On October 20, the Delhi Development Authority unveiled the Awas Nivesh Yojana 2026 to promote affordable housing initiatives. Within just two hours of its launch, over 2,500 flats targeted at the Low Income Group were booked online, thanks to a lucrative 25 percent discount. This scheme showcases a strong commitment to making quality housing attainable for families in need, reflecting the persistent demand for affordable options in Delhi.

news.title: Only 53 of over 2,400 PGs submitted structural safety certificates: Delhi civic body
news.para: In response to a recent collapse in Satya Niketan, the MCD conducted a survey of 2,457 PG accommodations to assess structural safety. Only 53 provided the necessary safety certificates before the deadline. This initiative aims to reduce risks and ensure adherence to building codes. With limited staff for audits, MCD plans to take action against violators next month and is developing stricter policies for older buildings.

news.title: NCDRC orders fresh completion certificates for Purab Premium Apartments
news.para: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has mandated Gmada to re-evaluate the completion certificates for Purab Premium Apartments. This ruling comes after addressing issues related to compensation and maintenance charges for residents. Gmada is required to confirm that all promised amenities are in place before issuing new certificates. Concerns have been raised by residents regarding the certificates issued back in October 2024.

news.title: Telangana housing minister distributes Indiramma housing sanction letters
news.para: Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy announced the continuation of the Indiramma housing scheme for eligible families in Telangana. The government has already sanctioned 4.5 lakh houses in the first phase and 2.5 lakh in the second phase. Nearly 2.4 lakh houses have been completed, with construction in rural areas ongoing. Despite financial challenges, the minister assured the announcement of further phases for housing.

news.title: Goa’s urban property card drive sees just 5% response
news.para: The state government has finished updating land records and has begun issuing urban property cards for landowners. Only 5% of landowners submitted documents for the new urban property cards after the recent survey. The survey, conducted using digital tools, was launched to update records since the last survey in 1972. Landowners who submitted their documents will be able to review their cards and raise objections if necessary.

news.title: Lucknow development body prepares to obtain approval for second phase of Naimish Nagar
news.para: The Lucknow Development Authority is gearing up to attain layout approval for the second phase of Naimish Nagar, which spans about 4,100 acres and is designed to include more than 20,000 plots. The first phase recorded a successful registration of 1,673 plots, continuing until October 24.

news.title: Over 1,500 illegal buildings flagged in Hyderabad in weeks
news.para: Hyderabad's municipal corporations are stepping up efforts to tackle illegal constructions following alarming incidents. Approximately 1,500 unauthorized structures have been pinpointed, leading to enhanced enforcement measures. The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation has demolished 500 buildings already, with GHMC identifying almost 500 additional violations. This rigorous crackdown focuses on closely scrutinizing construction progress to maintain safety standards and prevent unsafe developments from resurfacing in communities.

news.title: Gurugram: Brisk Lumbini residents asks DTCP to halt boundary wall plan
news.para: Residents of Brisk Lumbini have formally protested the developer's intentions to alter the boundary wall and introduce new shop entrances. They contend that these plans have not received proper authorization from the town planning department and infringe upon current building codes. Furthermore, they assert that these modifications would detrimentally impact communal spaces and services within the community.

news.title: UltraTech commissions ₹2,650-crore cement plant in Andhra Pradesh
news.para: UltraTech Cement has proudly inaugurated the Petnikota Cement Works located in Andhra Pradesh's Nandyal district. With an impressive investment of around Rs 2,650 crore, this facility boasts a remarkable manufacturing capacity. The plant is set to generate roughly 650 direct jobs along with 2,000 indirect ones. Notably, it harnesses renewable energy and operates without relying on groundwater or thermal power.

news.title: Sobha’s net profit declines 55% to ₹32.95 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: Sobha reported a 54.6 percent decline in net profit after tax for the quarter ending September 30, 2026. The company's total income also fell by 30.8 percent compared to the same period last year. However, real estate sales value increased by 16 percent year-on-year during the quarter. For the first half of FY27, Sobha achieved record sales value and positive collections.

news.title: UltraTech Cement's profit rises 21.3% to ₹1,501 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: During the September quarter, UltraTech Cement reported an impressive 21.27% increase in consolidated profit, reaching Rs 1,501.38 crore. This growth was fueled by an 18.81% rise in operational revenue, thanks to enhanced sales volumes and effective cost management. Domestic grey cement sales surged by 13.8%, solidifying the company's position in a competitive market, even as total expenses climbed by 18.44%.

news.title: Panchkula: 18-acre illegal colony razed in Golpura
news.para: On Sunday, a significant demolition operation unfolded in Golpura village as the district town planning department removed unauthorized structures in an illegal colony covering 18 acres. Under the leadership of DTP Babita Gupta, the operation was fortified by a strong police presence for safety. Officials reiterated that developing colonies requires prior approval and warned of ongoing enforcement against illegal construction throughout the district to address unauthorized colonization.

news.title: Farmers give consent, New Noida land acquisition set to begin soon
news.para: The Noida Authority is preparing to initiate land acquisition for New Noida, with 281 farmers already consenting to part with their plots. Finalized acquisition rates for the ambitious Dadri-Noida-Ghaziabad Investment Region, covering more than 20,000 hectares, are now in place. Planned in four phases, the aim is to secure 3,165 hectares by 2027.

news.title: Over 110 families in Kot Sekhon get property cards under ‘Mera Ghar, Mere Naam’ Scheme
news.para: Punjab cabinet minister Tarunpreet Singh Sond recently handed out property cards to 115 beneficiaries in Kot Sekhon village. This initiative aims to legally empower families who previously lacked clear ownership documentation. Utilizing surveys and digital mapping, these records will facilitate smoother access to bank loans and enhance future property transactions for generations to come.
